newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain bourse still seen setting more record highs.
newsitem.headline: Spain bourse still seen setting more record highs.

text.p: The Spanish stock market still has room to rise even after broad gains this year and a new high above 600 points in the Madrid General Index on Wednesday, analysts said.
"The market has room to continue rising and for the moment, one cannot talk of a ceiling," said Ignacio Gomez Montejo analyst at Merrill Lynch.
So far this year, the Madrid General Index has gained 35.4 percent, and the Ibex has risen 34.11 percent, both racing to a string of new historic highs.
The rise is partly attributed to strong cash inflows, seen continuing through the long-term, as interest rates have dropped.

"There are strong reasons to explain the bourse's movement, such as the constant flow of cash into stocks," said salesman Enrique Perez Pla of Schroeder. "There is potentially five trillion pesetas ($34.3 billion) ready to arrive, of which 1.5 trillion may have already come into stocks."
Fernando Chocarro, broker at AB Asesores, said "arrival of cash leads fund managers to buy without taking prices into account."
That flow from funds into stocks, mostly from domestic investors, has resulted from the fall in interest rates and expectations of further short-term rates cuts.
"There has been a change in traditional monetary asset investments," said Perez Pla. Lower rates have driven investors seeking higher returns into stocks.
Dealers also highlighted strong macro-economic data and profit forecasts as buoying shares.
"Besides the flow of cash, the bourse finds support in macro-economic indicators and good corporate profit forecasts," said Perez Pla.
On Wednesday, Spain said first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) rose 2.9 percent from year ago levels. GDP rose 2.6 percent in the final 1996 quarter.
Spain has also reported a strong rise in April industrial production and a significant drop in May unemployment, which helped convince economists that economic growth would continue to pick up.
Because the rise in indices has already outpaced most analysts' expectations, analysts were reluctant to predict when the market might top.
"We must start thinking about a balance when we reach a level 10 to 20 percent above the rest of Europe," said Gomez Montejo.
"The flow of money, the fall in short-term rates, the economic situation and market euphoria make it impossible to foresee levels," Chocarro said.
Amid the gains, dealers saw most potential in the banking sector.
"An economic pick-up favours banks, together with other consumer-linked companies, such as Cortefiel and, in the future, real estate firms," said Gomez Montejo.
"We are betting on the banking sector, which is giving broad growth levels without the effect as yet, of investment in Latin America coming through", Chocarro said.
